card.name: Fixed phrases in opioid label warnings
card.fires_on: The words "both" after "MAO inhibitors," and "progressing" after "somnolence" in opioid label text. They sit in repeated stock sentences about serotonin interactions and overdose presentation.

modes.label: Both after MAO inhibitors
modes.description: The word "both" follows a list of drugs that impair serotonin metabolism, ending in MAO inhibitors.
modes.example: drugs that impair metabolism of serotonin (including monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors,<< both>> those intended to treat psychiatric disorders and also

modes.label: Somnolence progressing
modes.description: The word "progressing" follows somnolence in the overdose clinical presentation sentence.
modes.example: Acute overdosage with buprenorphine is manifested by respiratory depression, somnolence<< progressing>> to stupor or coma, skeletal muscle

card.plain: It marks two stock phrases in opioid labels: the serotonin-interaction sentence and the overdose symptoms sentence.
